correctness.rationale: Let Σ=S³/I* be the Poincaré integral homology sphere, with |I*|=120 and covering S³→Σ of degree 120. A degree-one collapse u:Σ→S³ is integral homology isomorphism but not a homotopy equivalence; after triangulation and simplicial approximation use face-poset map φ#. In P^{(m)} the first m stages are F(K), then Q=F(L), while target Q remains constant. All homology transition maps are isomorphisms, so d_I=0. An explicit m-interleaving gives d_HC≤m. For ε<m the interleaving identity at index zero would give maps S³→Σ→S³ with composite degree 1; every map S³→Σ has degree divisible by 120, contradiction. For each lower-set fiber, the 2⌈m/2⌉-shift lands in the contractible poset L_v, so the structure maps are nullhomotopic and the compatible point-selection supplies weak ε-contractibility (face-poset image meets every target vertex because its degree is one). This is an exact general-m construction, not finite evidence.

originality.rationale: Guzeev–Tanaka establish the persistent Quillen–McCord upper bound from weakly ε-contractible fibers and compare homology with homotopy interleaving. They do not state an exact all-m counterfamily with d_I=0 and d_HC=m at fixed target in the relevant examined theorem and discussion; the delay construction using a homology sphere is a substantive difference from their general bound. Published related finite-poset results were searched for equivalence or domination. Priority remains best-of-knowledge.
